hook: Pricing freelance work at your old salary's hourly rate?

blocks.narration: Pricing freelance work at your old salary's hourly rate? You are quietly working for less money than before. Here is why.
blocks.visual: Bold poster-style graphic of a stopwatch with a price tag hanging from it, orange and navy palette

blocks.narration: A sixty thousand dollar salary works out to about twenty-nine dollars an hour, based on roughly two thousand eighty work hours a year.
blocks.visual: A calendar grid of work hours fills up block by block

blocks.narration: But freelancers almost never bill every hour. Emails, pitching clients, invoicing, and admin all take time nobody pays for.
blocks.visual: Some blocks in the grid turn gray, labeled with tiny envelope and paperwork icons

blocks.narration: If sixty percent of your time is billable, that is only about twelve hundred fifty paid hours a year.
blocks.visual: The grid shrinks as the gray blocks fall away, leaving fewer orange blocks

blocks.narration: To earn the same sixty thousand dollars, you would need about forty-eight dollars an hour, and that is before other costs.
blocks.visual: A price tag on the stopwatch flips upward to a higher number

blocks.narration: Then add self-employment tax, health insurance, retirement savings, software, and equipment that an employer used to cover for you.
blocks.visual: Small icons stack on a scale: a medical cross, a piggy bank, a laptop

blocks.narration: That is why many freelancers land near double their old hourly rate. It is not greed, it is covering the full cost of working.
blocks.visual: The scale balances once the price tag doubles, a satisfied click

blocks.narration: Price for the business you actually run. Comment your field and I will make a video on its rates.
blocks.visual: The figure confidently hands over an invoice as the camera pulls back

cta: Comment your field and I will make a video on its rates.

captions.hook_line: If you charge your old salary's hourly rate as a freelancer, you're losing money 📉
captions.body: $60,000 a year is about $29 an hour at 2,080 work hours. Freelancers rarely bill every hour; at 60% billable that is about 1,250 hours, so the same income needs roughly $48 an hour before self-employment tax, benefits and tools. Many land near double the old hourly rate.

youtube_title: Why Freelancers Should Charge Double Their Old Hourly Pay
